answer.rationale: With 14 days to expiry and the line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, any action that introduces migration or qualification work (switch_primary_vendor, add_second_source) buys cost at the direct expense of delivery risk, which the objective forbids; defer_decision (memory_c5) worked only because that renewal was non-critical and had month-to-month fallback, neither of which holds here since this contract does not auto-renew. That leaves incumbent-facing options, and negotiate_terms dominates plain renewal because it captures the same continuity benefit (memory_c1) while attacking price, and can be combined with the volume/multi-year lever that previously cut unit cost without narrowing scope (memory_c6). I verify memory_c4 rather than memory_c2 because c4 is the memory my action actually rests on, and its stated outcome is qualitative: 'recovered real margin' tells me the direction but not the magnitude, and I need to know whether the recovery was low-single-digit or approached the 18% finance now demands, plus whether the benchmarking leverage came from conditions (credible alternate bids, slack volume) that exist today. I do not verify memory_c2 because even if the low-cost switch outcome is confirmed exactly as recorded, the fast onboarding it describes happened without a 14-day cliff and without a zero-buffer line, so it cannot change this cycle's choice. Caveats I am carrying forward rather than resolving: all six memories are outcome-only survivor records with no failed-negotiation or failed-switch counterexamples, so the apparent reliability of incumbent-facing moves may be selection effect; and if renegotiation lands short of 18%, closing the gap by price pressure alone risks the incumbent quietly trimming expedite responsiveness or allocation priority, degrading the delivery reliability that is the whole reason for staying, so I would rather book a partial cost win plus a shorter term with benchmark reopeners and start second-source qualification next review than force the full cut now.
